subject: Hosted commit increase & tier split — SurgePath renewal
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@surgepath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: SurgePath hosted commit increase & rate-split

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, SurgePath's usage has been steadily exceeding your current monthly commit, and you asked for a proposal that both lowers unit cost and preserves predictable throughput during peak workflows.

Summary of what we propose:
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 24 months for improved economics)
- Baseline monthly commit: 1.2B tokens/month (up from 600M)
- Tiered rate bands (see attached rate_table_surges_v2.csv): lower per-token price up to commit, a soft-burst allowance of 15% at reduced surcharge, and a higher overage price beyond that.
- Rate split: 70% of baseline at Tier A price, remainder at Tier B.
- Ops: Dedicated on-call during planned campaign spikes; auto-burst routing enabled.

Attached is a draft Mutual Action & Acceptance Plan (MAAP) capturing timelines, milestones, and a starter SOW. This is intentionally lightweight so procurement and your engineering leads can move quickly.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm whether 1.2B/month aligns with your forecast for Q4.
2) If yes, we’ll lock in a 30-day provisional provisioning window and send a DocuSign with the MAAP/Commit Amendment for signature.

If procurement needs alternative billing cadence (quarterly vs monthly) we can accommodate — mention that in reply and we’ll include changes in the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SurgePath_MAAP_draft_v1.pdf (pdf stub), rate_table_surges_v2.csv (csv stub)
From: Daniel Cho <daniel@surgepath.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: SurgePath Procurement <procurement@surgepath.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: SurgePath hosted commit increase & rate-split

Monica,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from procurement and our infra lead:
- Can you share concrete $/1M-token numbers for Tier A and Tier B (and the overage surcharge)? Procurement needs these for the PO.
- For the soft-burst 15%: what is the enforcement window (minute/hour/day) and how does that interact with rate limiting?
- If we go with 12 months and hit 130% sustained usage for 3 months, is there an automatic re-rate or will that trigger a review?
- Billing cadence: procurement prefers quarterly invoicing for now. Any blockers?

Engineering note: our SRE asked that KV cache warming + prefix-caching be included as part of the onboarding checklist for the provisioning window. Can you loop in ops for that?

If the numbers look good we can move fast — procurement ready to raise a PO within 5 business days once we have the signed MAAP and the billable rates.

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Head of Platform, SurgePath
daniel@surgepath.com | +1 (617) 555-4021

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SurgePath pricing options (do not forward)

Monica / Ben,

Quick internal note before I respond to Daniel with the numbers. Two viable commercial levers here:

Option A (12mo, conservative uplift)
- Baseline commit: 1.2B tokens/mo
- Tier A: $28 / 1M tokens up to commit
- Tier B: $40 / 1M tokens between commit and commit+15% (soft-burst)
- Overage: $70 / 1M tokens beyond commit+15%
- Quarterly invoicing ok; finance reviewed margin at ~28% after infra and support credits

Option B (24mo, better discount)
- Baseline commit: 1.2B tokens/mo
- Tier A: $24 / 1M tokens up to commit
- Tier B: $36 / 1M tokens soft-burst
- Overage: $60 / 1M tokens beyond soft-burst
- Add a 10% prepayment discount on first two quarters if they prepurchase credits

Operational controls:
- Soft-burst window: rolling 60-minute window aggregated per account, with automatic KV/prefix cache warming allowed for 30 minutes after a sudden traffic surge.
- If usage >=130% sustained for 90 days -> trigger a formal cadence review (no automatic re-rate without signed amendment).

Recommend we lead with Option A in the reply (conservative) and offer Option B if they request longer term — call out DocuSign paths for both.

Ben — can you confirm the ops onboarding checklist is ok for the 60-minute rolling enforcement? Also confirm on-call coverage for the provisioning week.

Karthik
Director, Revenue Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@surgepath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: SurgePath hosted commit increase & rate-split

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the questions. We discussed internally and offering the conservative starter so procurement can move quickly. Full answers below and the updated DocuSign link at the bottom.

Rates (Option A, 12 months):
- Tier A: $28 / 1M tokens (applies up to the committed 1.2B tokens/mo)
- Tier B (soft-burst band up to +15%): $40 / 1M tokens
- Overage (beyond commit+15%): $70 / 1M tokens

Soft-burst enforcement:
- Rolling 60-minute window per account. If usage stays above commit+15% for more than 60 minutes, charges flow to the overage band and we notify SRE and account owner. During a spike we enable a 30-minute cache-warmup allowance to reduce cold starts.

Sustained spike policy:
- If you exceed 130% of the commit for 90 consecutive days we will open a review with your account team. There is no automatic re-rate — any permanent change requires an amendment.

Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing is supported. We will include quarterly invoice terms in the DocuSign.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/SurgePath-Commit-6721 (temporary link)

If this aligns, tell procurement to expect a DocuSign from Redwood Legal (cc’d Lauren for contract intake) and we’ll provision the additional capacity within the 30-day provisional window once signatures are complete.

Best,
Monica

Monica,

Thanks — those numbers are clear and procurement confirms quarterly invoicing is acceptable. We reviewed the MAAP and the legal team is comfortable with the scope in the draft.

We will proceed with Option A (12mo, 1.2B/mo). Procurement will raise the PO today and I’ll route it to Lauren for signature on the DocuSign. Can you confirm who to send the PO to for invoicing and whether we should include a purchase order number in the DocuSign metadata?

Also: please add a short ops onboarding note in the MAAP to call out the KV cache warmup step (so our infra lead can tick the box during provisioning).

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Daniel
